project: Web Design Suite — email compile target
about: This is the email-safe PROJECTION of the token system, not a second token system.
tokens.css remains the source of truth. This file is generated from it by hand (or by
a project's own export step) and every value here traces back to one there.
survives    — the role exists in email with the same meaning; only the notation changed
substituted — the role exists but the VALUE had to change because email cannot express
the original notation (oklch, clamp, calc, box-shadow). Every one carries
dropped     — the role has no email meaning at all. Listed in `dropped` below with what
to use instead, so that a template referencing it fails loudly at build
time rather than silently rendering nothing.
Density is resolved at build time. tokens.css multiplies every spacing role by
var(--density); email has no runtime dial, so these values are the --density:1 resolution.
To ship a compact variant, export a second tokens file, do not add a dial to the template.

substitution_policy.oklch-to-hex: No email client resolves oklch(). Every colour is the sRGB hex of the exact same oklch() value from tokens.css, computed with the standard OKLab matrices. Hex, not rgb(), because the Outlook Word engine and several mobile clients handle 3/6-digit hex most reliably and hex is the only colour notation that survives every client in the matrix.
substitution_policy.clamp-to-fixed: clamp() and any viewport unit are unsupported in the Word engine and unreliable elsewhere. Fluid steps collapse to the DESKTOP anchor, and the mobile size comes back via a media query on a class, not via the token.
substitution_policy.rem-to-px: The Word engine converts some lengths to points and leaves others in pixels, and rem has no reliable root to resolve against in an email body. Every length is px.
substitution_policy.calc-removed: calc() is unsupported in the Word engine and in Gmail. All arithmetic (the density multiply, the fluid interpolation) is done here, at build time.
substitution_policy.shorthand-font-removed: The `font: weight size/leading family` shorthand is mis-parsed by several clients and by the Word engine in particular. The --type-* roles are exported as size/line/weight/family triples instead.
substitution_policy.shadow-to-edge: box-shadow is ignored by the Word engine and stripped or flattened elsewhere. Elevation becomes a 1px border (--email-edge) or, where real depth is wanted, a table-based shadow built from two nested cells. See references/email-architecture.md §5.
substitution_policy.webfont-to-stack: Web fonts do not load in the Word engine, Gmail (beyond Roboto/Google Sans) or several mobile clients, and a @font-face that half-loads is worse than one that never does. The font roles are websafe stacks. A brand face may be layered on top via @font-face in the retained <style> block — but the stack must stand alone.

--bg-canvas.note: the outer wrapper table's bgcolor — the area around the 600px container

--bg-sunken.note: wells, the footer band, receipt totals row

--bg-selected.note: callout tint; no selection exists in email, kept for the tint value

--bg-raised.note: identical to --bg-surface in email because the shadow that distinguished them is gone. Use --email-edge to separate them.

--fg-subtle.contrast: 4.90:1 on --bg-canvas, 4.57:1 on --bg-sunken — at the floor, do not lighten

--bg-accent.note: the CTA fill. 600 not 500, for the same reason as on the web: white on 500 is 3.56:1 and a button label is small text.

--bg-accent-hover.note: no :hover in Gmail or the Word engine. Kept only for the webmail clients where a retained :hover rule can use it.

--space-section.note: the 144px desktop anchor is absurd in a 600px column. Section rhythm in email is set by the column, not the viewport: 48px desktop, 32px on phones via .m-section in the media query.

--gutter-page.note: the container's left/right padding. 24px desktop, 20px on phones.

--font-sans.value: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
--font-sans.note: system-ui is omitted: the Word engine does not resolve it and falls back to Times New Roman, which is the single most common 'why does this email look like a 1998 memo' cause.

--font-mono.value: Consolas, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Monaco, 'Courier New', monospace

--text-3xl.note: rounded down from 35px: a 600px column cannot carry 35px headings without awkward wraps, and 32px keeps the 8px grid the Word engine rounds to anyway.

--text-5xl.note: collapsed to the clamp MINIMUM, not the maximum: the maximum (72px) assumes a viewport, and email has a 600px column.

--leading-none.note: unitless leading is honoured everywhere in the matrix; px leading is only needed on spacer cells

--tracking-tight.note: em tracking is honoured in WebKit/Chromium clients and silently ignored by the Word engine. Harmless either way.

--weight-medium.note: value unchanged. SF, first in the stack, has a 500; Segoe UI and Arial (classic Outlook's font) do not, and render it as 400. Use 700 when weight must be visible everywhere.

--weight-semibold.note: SF and Segoe UI, which lead the stack, have a semibold; Arial, classic Outlook's font, does not and renders 600 as bold

--type-display-line.note: px leading, not 1.15: the Word engine rounds unitless leading unpredictably at display sizes

--type-h1-size.note: email's own heading scale for a 600px column (display 44px, h1 32px, h2 24px, h3 20px), not tokens.css's fluid steps

--type-h2-size.note: email's own heading scale for a 600px column (display 44px, h1 32px, h2 24px, h3 20px), not tokens.css's fluid steps

--type-h2-weight.note: 600 in tokens.css; 700 here, so the heading has the same weight in classic Outlook's Arial, which has no 600, as everywhere else

--type-body-size.note: never smaller. iOS Mail auto-enlarges text under 13px and breaks the layout doing it.

--type-ui-size.note: bumped from 14px: the only --type-ui in email is a button label, and a 14px label inside a 44px tap target reads as an afterthought on a phone.

--type-label-size.note: bumped from 12px to meet email's own 13px floor. An uppercase tracked eyebrow at 12px is the single most common thing iOS Mail auto-enlarges, and it does it to that element alone — so the eyebrow grows and the heading beneath it does not. lint_email.py enforces the same floor; the token file and the linter must not disagree.

--type-legal-size.note: 11px legal text is below the iOS Mail auto-enlarge floor and fails contrast perception for many readers. Email's floor is 13px.

--radius-sm.note: ignored by the Word engine — corners render square there. Acceptable degradation; do not chase it with images.

--radius-full.note: 999px not 9999px — VML arcsize is a percentage and a 9999px pill and a 999px pill are identical at email scale, but some clients clamp large radii oddly.

--email-width.note: the container width. 600px is not superstition: it is the widest that fits the classic Outlook reading pane at 100% zoom on a 1024px-wide window without a horizontal scrollbar.

--email-width-inner.note: --email-width minus two --gutter-page. Ghost tables and full-bleed images use this.

--email-bp-stack.note: the one media-query breakpoint. Below this, two-column rows stack.

--email-edge.note: one token for the whole shorthand, resolved at build time, so the client receives `1px solid #e7e5e2` and a change to --border-subtle reaches it.

--email-button-pad.note: tuned so the padded anchor's rendered box is 48px tall at --type-ui-size/line — above --email-tap-min with room for the Word engine's rounding.

--email-dark-canvas.note: Dark-treatment hints, honoured by Apple Mail and Thunderbird and ignored by most of the matrix. These are TOKENS for the same reason the light roles are: a hand-written #1a1a1a in a dark-mode block is exactly the drift the contract exists to stop.

--email-dark-fg-muted.note: n300, not the light theme's n600 mirrored. Dark surfaces need MORE lightness separation, same finding as tokens.css records for the web dark theme.

--email-dark-link.note: accent-300 not accent-400: 400 is 6.92:1 which passes, but link text sits inside body copy at 16px and the extra headroom costs nothing.

--density.reason: No runtime dial. calc() is unsupported in the Word engine and Gmail. Every spacing role here is the --density:1 resolution; export a second tokens file for a compact variant.

--bg-hover.reason: Gmail and the Word engine strip :hover entirely; a hover state that works for a third of readers is a liability, not a feature.
--bg-hover.use: nothing — design the resting state to be obviously clickable

--bg-active.reason: No :active in any client in the matrix.

--bg-disabled.reason: Nothing in an email can be disabled.

--fg-disabled.reason: Nothing in an email can be disabled.

--border-focus.reason: No focus ring survives; the client owns focus styling for links.

--border-invalid.reason: No form fields in email, so nothing is ever invalid.

--shadow-xs.reason: box-shadow ignored by the Word engine, flattened elsewhere.

--shadow-sm.reason: box-shadow ignored by the Word engine.

--shadow-md.reason: box-shadow ignored by the Word engine.
--shadow-md.use: --email-edge, or the table-based shadow in email-architecture.md §5

--shadow-lg.reason: box-shadow ignored by the Word engine.

--shadow-xl.reason: box-shadow ignored by the Word engine.

--elevation-focus.reason: The focus ring is a box-shadow, which Outlook's Word engine drops; links in email keep the client's own focus style.

--bg-scrim.reason: Nothing overlays anything in email, so there is nothing to dim.

--dur-instant.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--dur-fast.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--dur-base.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--dur-slow.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--dur-slower.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--ease-out.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--ease-in.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--ease-in-out.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--ease-spring.reason: No transitions or animations survive the matrix.

--z-base.reason: position is stripped by Gmail and unsupported by the Word engine; there is no stacking context to index.

--bp-sm.reason: One breakpoint only. Email has one layout change (stack/unstack), not five.

--measure-prose.reason: ch units are unsupported in the Word engine; measure in email is fixed by --email-width-inner, which at --type-body-size is about 62 characters — inside the readable band by construction.

--width-form.reason: No forms in email. A form that posts from an inbox is stripped by most clients and flagged as phishing by the rest.

--grid-columns.reason: No grid. Columns are table cells.

--type-h4.reason: font shorthand, and a 600px column does not need four heading levels.

--text-6xl.reason: A 72px headline in a 600px column wraps to three lines on a phone.

--space-24.reason: Above 80px, vertical space in a 600px column reads as a bug rather than as rhythm.

--space-0-5.reason: 2px optical gaps are below the Word engine's rounding resolution — it will render 0 or 4px unpredictably.

[data-theme=\"dark\"].reason: There is no dark THEME in email, only client-applied dark TREATMENT. No client reads a data-theme attribute you set. The dark palette is therefore not a re-pointing of these roles; it is a set of hints (meta color-scheme, a prefers-color-scheme block, [data-ogsc] overrides) that three clients honour and the rest ignore. See references/email-client-matrix.md §8 — you do not get to pick the colours, you get to influence them.
